title: Spelling List 4
ruleLine: ten of these fourteen words are Latin words that change their ending, not their beginning, to go from one to many.
chartBtn: singulars and plurals side by side

tips.listen: Listen right to the end — the ending is the rule this week.
tips.boxes: Remember the rule — it is the ending that changes, not the beginning.
tips.reveal: The ending is in pink. That is the part the test is looking for.
tips.plain: No Latin ending on this one — it is a root or teacher's-choice word.

chart.head: One of them
chart.note: the singular. Latin endings — a, on, um.

chart.head: More than one
chart.note: the plural. Same word, new ending — ae, a, a.

chart.head: Root and teacher's choice
chart.note: flam = fire, and two the teacher chose.

words.def: a girl or woman who has attended or graduated from a particular school, college, or university
words.sent: The school invited one ___ back to speak at the assembly about her career.

words.def: more than one girl or woman who has attended or graduated from a particular school, college, or university
words.sent: Four ___ came back for the reunion and sat together in the front row.

words.def: facts or situations that are observed to exist or happen, especially ones whose cause or explanation is in question
words.sent: Lightning and rainbows are two ___ that people once had no way to explain.

words.def: a fact or situation that is observed to exist or happen, especially one whose cause or explanation is in question
words.sent: The northern lights are a ___ that scientists still study closely.
A single ___ tells you almost nothing until you have hundreds more to compare.

words.def: facts and statistics collected together for reference or analysis
words.sent: The class collected rainfall ___ every morning for a month.

words.def: more than one lesson plan, each one made up of different subjects
words.sent: The two schools follow different ___, so their fifth graders read different books.

words.def: the subjects that make up a course of study in a school or college
words.sent: Fifth grade has a full ___ of math, science, history, and reading.

words.def: written statements, records, or communications, such as within an office
words.sent: The principal's folder was stuffed with ___ from the district office.

words.def: a written message in business and diplomacy
words.sent: Ana's mother wrote a short ___ to remind everyone about the meeting.

words.def: meant to stir up angry or violent feelings
words.sent: The coach warned the team not to post anything ___ about the other side.

words.def: a tall wading bird with pink or scarlet feathers and long legs and neck
words.sent: A ___ stands on one leg for hours without ever losing its balance.

words.def: a person one knows slightly, but who is not a close friend
words.sent: Jamal knew the man from the bus stop, but he was only an ___.

words.def: to be quick to do something, or to move and travel hurriedly
words.sent: If we ___ we can still catch the ferry before it leaves.
